title: Council facing budget black hole due to 'unprecedented demand' to support children in care
excerpt: The ‘unprecedented demand’ of children in care with ‘complex needs’ has led to forecast overspends in a number of areas, officials have said.
content:
The ‘unprecedented demand’ of children in care with ‘complex needs’ has led to forecast overspends in a number of areas, officials have said.

Members of Lincolnshire County Council’s audit committee were told that the increase in the number of complex children in care is causing the council to overspend in this budget area.

This comes after councillors were previously told that it can cost the authority up to £18,000 a week to support a child in care with complex needs.

This has resulted in a forecast overspend of £12.6 million between April and June this year.

At a meeting on Monday, September 21, Pam Clipson, head of financial services at LCC, said: “For me, it’s the unprecedented demand that we’re seeing in some of our areas - children in care in particular - so we haven’t got them across the board.

“Children in care is playing out in a number of areas, being homeschooled and transport, particularly in the SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) area - which is linked.

“It is also playing out in some of our other children’s related services and how they transition from children to adults.”

Coun Cain Parkinson (Conservative - Grantham East) called on the authority to look at how these overspends could be reduced.

He said: “What we’re seeing is quite significant overspends in a number of areas.

“So is it something that we as a council need to look at into how we do those forecasts on the potential spends in those portfolios to make sure that they consistently deliver based on what the actual spending is, rather than having consistent overspends in different budget areas.”

Andrew Middleton, an independent member, explained that it’s difficult for the council to budget for children in care, because the situation is difficult to predict.

He said: “The significant problem is none of us have control over demand. None of us has control over complexity of need.

“The difference between a moderate need and a higher level need can be three, four, five thousand a week.

“You don’t need that many patients with that level of need to add up to an awful lot of money.”
